subject: Post-demo: Sigmax RAG evaluation & staging plan

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@sigmaxhealth.com>, Alex Meyer <ameyer@sigmaxhealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: Sigmax RAG evaluation & staging plan

Thanks again for the demo time earlier today — appreciate the thorough walkthrough of the clinical search workflow. Per our conversation, I captured a compact plan for the staging evaluation (focused on model fit + grounding metrics) and a handful of recommendations we think will surface the most informative signals for Sigmax. See the short summary + next steps below.

High-level recommendation (what to run in staging):
- Candidate models: redwood-chat-3b-quant (cost-efficient baseline), redwood-chat-13b (balanced latency/quality), and an experimental run using open-mistral-7b-instruct with a stronger reranker to understand recall/precision tradeoffs.
- Retrieval: dense embeddings + FAISS store; chunking ~400–600 tokens (source docs are long clinical notes).
- Reranking: evaluate cross-encoder for top-30 re-rank (high-precision use case), and a bi-encoder rerank baseline for cost comparison.
- Benchmarks & prompts: use the attached prompt_suite_sigmax_v1.jsonl (clinical-QA, instruction-style prompts, and ambiguous-query probes). We also added a small regression prompt set to catch common hallucination cases.

RAG-specific eval metrics we will capture:
- grounding_rate (% of responses that cite a retrieved doc/span)
- hallucination_rate (manual labels on the probe set)
- answer_fidelity (F1 against labeled answers on clinical-QA set)
- latency P50/P95 token-level and end-to-end
- cost per 1k requests (estimated)

Initial staging config (recommended):
- Retriever: dense ANN (HNSW index) with top_k_retriever=150
- Chunk size: 500 tokens, stride 100, keep doc metadata (author/date/source) for filtering
- Reranker: cross-encoder re-rank top_n=30 (we'll also run bi-encoder-only baseline)
- Prompting: supply 3 retrieved passages + system instruction enforcing source citations

Attachments & links:
- prompt_suite_sigmax_v1.jsonl (attached) — prompt categories + expected labels
- runtimes_benchmarks_sigmax.csv (we'll attach sample runtime/cost runs after initial config)
- Eval harness (internal): https://git.redwood.com/eval-harness/sigmax-clinical-qa

Proposed next steps / owners:
1) Engineering kickoff for staging dataset ingestion — Connor O'Brien (Connor) — target: Tue 2027-05-25
2) Run initial model sweep (3 candidate models) and collect metrics — Soojin Lee (Soojin) — target: Thu 2027-05-28
3) Share initial results + short triage on hallucination probes — Rachel Kim (me) — target: Fri 2027-05-29
4) Decide canary / pilot criteria (grounding_rate >= 0.9 on high-priority probes AND acceptable latency) — joint decision w/ Sigmax

If that plan looks good I'll send the calendar invite for a staging kickoff and upload a small sample (10 docs) of the dataset so Soojin can confirm chunking.

Thanks —

Hi all — quick technical clarifications and what I'll run for the initial sweep: 

Retriever / index notes:
- We'll use dense embeddings generated with redwood-embed-384 and store in FAISS using HNSW for fast recall; given corpus size (~125k notes) HNSW is a good latency/cost sweet spot.
- Chunking: 400–600 tokens (I recommend 500 tokens with 100 token overlap). That preserves context while keeping index vectors compact.
- Metadata filters: add filters for doc_type (note, discharge_summary) and source_system (EHR-v2) so we can quickly exclude low-value doc types during early tests.

Retrieval + rerank pipeline:
- Retriever top_k=150; candidate pool will then be reranked with a cross-encoder (re-rank top_n=30). Cross-encoder yields better grounding precision (we expect +8–12% over bi-encoder-only on clinical-QA) but costs ~3–4x tokens for reranking.
- For a cost/latency baseline, I'll also produce a bi-encoder-only run with distillation-retriever rerank (cheap) so we can compare cost-per-query.

Scoring thresholds & metrics capture:
- grounding_precision: fraction of answers where the top-cited span overlaps a labeled supporting span — target >= 0.90 for high-confidence flows
- hallucination_probe_score: manual binary label on a 120-probe set (we'll compute % hallucination) — aim < 0.08 initially
- reranker_confidence_cut: for cross-encoder we'll record the softmax score distribution; propose an operational cutoff at 0.65 to force fallback to human review for low-confidence answers.

Practical notes:
- Reranker model: I'll start with redwood-cross-qa-1.0 (fine-tuned for factual ranking).
- Batch sizing: continuous batching likely won't affect the retrieval step but will help generation latency; I'll surface per-token latency P50/P95 for each model.
- Deliverable: CSV with per-probe rows (probe_id, model, grounding_flag, hallucination_flag, latency_ms, cost_usd) — I'll attach a sample CSV once the first sweep completes.

I'll kick off the indexing job once Connor uploads the 10-doc sample Rachel mentioned.

— Soojin
